slotReserved.headline: {fieldName} took column {column}
slotReserved.detail: The reserver picked it — you did not, and could not. It is {status}{pageInfo}.

fieldIndexed.headline: {fieldName} is indexed
fieldIndexed.detail: The backfill finished and the slot flipped to ready. The filter that was refused a moment ago now returns rows.

retypeStarted.detailDemote: Its column is tombstoned. The residue stays there until the Liberator sweeps it, and only then can it be reserved again.
retypeStarted.detailWaiting: It is marked filterable with no slot behind it — nothing was free. The Watcher has to provision a page before the backfill can start.
retypeStarted.detailIndexing: A slot is reserved and backfilling. Filters on it are refused for the whole of that window, which is the point of it.

exhaustionFallback.headline: A write outran its index
exhaustionFallback.detail: Entry {entryId} is stored in full — the payload is the system of record. It is queued for a slot the Reconciler will reserve.

dlqInserted.headline: Entry {entryId} was quarantined
dlqInserted.detail: {reason} — kept in the DLQ rather than dropped, and replayable.

rejectionReasons.fieldUnknown: There is no field called {fieldName} on this model.
rejectionReasons.fieldNotFilterableBuilding: {fieldName} is mid-backfill. A half-built index is refused rather than answered from, which is why this is an error and not an empty result.
rejectionReasons.fieldNotFilterableNoSlot: {fieldName} has no slot behind it. The registry may well say it is filterable — that is intent, and a filter needs an index.
rejectionReasons.valueTypeMismatch: The value given for {fieldName} is the wrong type for its declared type.
rejectionReasons.valueOutOfBounds: The value given for {fieldName} is outside the bounds the wire format allows.
rejectionReasons.sortFieldUnknown: You cannot sort by {fieldName} — there is no such field on this model.
rejectionReasons.sortFieldNotSortable: {fieldName} has no live slot, so there is no index to sort it by.
rejectionReasons.cursorSortMismatch: The cursor was minted under a different ordering. Walking it now would silently page through a different sequence.

renameStarted.headline: {oldName} is now {newName}
renameStarted.detail: The registry changed instantly; every stored payload is still on the old key. Reads bridge the gap, filters on {oldName} do not.

renameComplete.headline: Every row is on {newName} now
renameComplete.detail: The backfill finished and previous_name is null again. The read fallback is retired — nothing needs it, because nothing is behind.

fieldSevered.headline: {fieldName} is gone from every read
fieldSevered.detail: Severance is instant and total — reads, filters, exports and describeModel() all stop seeing it. Its values are still sitting in entry_data until the purge reaches them.

fieldPurged.headline: {fieldName} is fully purged
fieldPurged.detail: The last chunk removed the key from every payload and dropped the registry row with it. The name is reusable again — it was not, while the row still held it.

modelSevered.headline: {modelName} has gone dark
modelSevered.detail: Severed along with all {fieldCount} of its fields. Reads return nothing — not an error, nothing, exactly as for a model that never existed — and writes are refused rather than stripped.

modelPurged.headline: Model {modelId} and its rows are gone
modelPurged.detail: The purge deleted the entries themselves, not just keys, and the final chunk dropped the model row. Nothing retains them.

columnReclaimed.headline: A tombstoned column is clear
columnReclaimed.detail: Slot {slotId} swept to the end of the page. The column holds no residue and is free for the next reservation.
